title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Grothendieck's late-1970s and early-1980s work on Teichmüller groupoids, i.e. finite presentations of fundamental groupoids of moduli spaces M_{g,ν} with respect to a family of base points. Here the base points are indexed combinatorially by a map (carte). R is the set of flags or 'repères' of the map, acted on by permutations σ0 and σ1. The page writes ω = σ0σ1, so σ1σ0 = ω^{-1}. A is the set of ω-orbits (the faces or cycles a of the map). Generating arrows ã_r, b̃_r, c̃_r, d̃_r are attached to each flag r.

The page states the 'remaining' defining relations of the groupoid H:
- (1) Relation (1) is a 4-term = 2-term cell relation: ã_r b̃_r c̃_r d̃_r = b̃_{r1} c̃_{r2}, with r1 = σ0(r) and r2 = σ1σ0(r) = ω^{-1}(r). It is a pentagon/hexagon-type relation, but on flags.
- (2') Put Ã_r := b̃_r^{-1} ã_r^{-1} b̃_{r1}. Relation (2') is an equality of two ω-orbit products: Ã_{ω^m r''}…Ã_{r''} = Ã_{ω^m r1}…Ã_{r1}, with r'' = ω(r). This is required for all a ∈ A, and m+1 is presumably the length of the orbit.

Grothendieck then introduces loop elements as products along orbits:
- μ_{Q̃_a} := Ã_{ω^m r''}…Ã_{r''}.
- μ_{R̃_r} := B̃_{ω^m r}…B̃_r, with B̃_r := ã_{r''}^{-1} b̃_{r1} b̃_r^{-1} (reading uncertain).
- μ_{P̃^ω_a} := d̃_{ω^m r''}…d̃_{r''}.

From these he defines λ_X := μ_{X^∨} μ_X, a product of the μ for an object and for its 'dual' a^∨ (r^∨). These look like full twists (Dehn twists) built as a product of two 'half' loops.

The conclusion sketched is twofold:
- The relations (3), (4), (5) are 'commutation' relations of the arrows ã, b̃, c̃.
- The 'transport' relations (8), (9), (10) are automatic, or reduce to (1) and (2); the left-margin crossed-out note mentions '6 relations équivalentes'. They amount to commutation of the arrows ã_r, b̃_r, c̃_r with the λ's.

In modern terms: the twist loops λ define natural (central-type) automorphisms of the groupoid, compatible with all generating arrows, as Dehn twists along boundary or cut curves are in a mapping class groupoid. The goal is a minimal presentation of a Teichmüller groupoid indexed by the flags of a map, with relations of 'cell' type (1), (2') plus twist-commutation relations.
errors: The line λ_{Q̃} = μ_{Q̃_{a^∨}} μ_{Q̃_a} = Ã_{ω^m r''}…Ã_{r''} = Ã_{ω^m r1}…Ã_{r1} cannot be literally right. A product of two μ's is set equal to a single orbit product, which is just (2'). Probably the right side is meant to identify μ_{Q_{a^∨}} with the r1-side product, or the equality is a slip.
The index m is not specified. Presumably m+1 is the length of the ω-orbit, so it depends on a (or r).
The first boxed (2') at the top uses 'r_{μ+1}'-like indices and writes '−' signs that are probably product dots. It is an earlier draft of the boxed (2') below.
The definition of B̃_r and the exact index pattern (r'' vs r1) are hard to read and may be inconsistent with Ã_r. Without pages defining (3)–(10), the claimed implications cannot be checked.

ideas.what: Presentation of a (Teichmüller-type) groupoid with generators indexed by the flags R of a combinatorial map and relations indexed by orbits of σ0, σ1, ω=σ0σ1
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial presentation of mapping class groupoids via ribbon graphs / maps (cf. Hatcher–Thurston complex, Penner/Harer ribbon-graph cell decompositions, Moore–Seiberg-type groupoids)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hatcher–Thurston (1980), Harer (1986), Penner (1987), Moore–Seiberg (1989), Bakalov–Kirillov (2000), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) describes the Teichmüller tower and its generation in low modular dimension, but not this flag-indexed presentation

ideas.what: Loop elements μ defined as ordered products of generators around an ω-orbit (face/vertex cycle)
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy / holonomy around a cycle of a ribbon graph; half-twist-type elements

ideas.what: λ = μ_{a^∨}·μ_a as twist elements, and transport relations equivalent to commutation of all generating arrows with the λ's
ideas.modern_name: Dehn twists along boundary curves being central / natural automorphisms of the mapping class groupoid (twists commuting with moves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Dehn, Birman); in groupoid form Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov

ideas.what: Reduction: transport relations (8)–(10) are automatic or follow from the cell relations (1), (2')
ideas.modern_name: Elimination of redundant relations in a groupoid presentation

missed.claim: A specific explicit presentation of a Teichmüller groupoid with base points indexed by the flags of a map (dessin). Generators ã, b̃, c̃, d̃ per flag; a 4=2 cell relation (1) and an orbit relation (2'); twist elements λ = μ^∨μ; transport relations reduced to commutation with λ. This presentation does not appear in this form in the published literature on Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower.
missed.quote: ã_r b̃_r c̃_r d̃_r = b̃_{r1} c̃_{r2} ... où on pose Ã_r = b̃_r^{-1} ã_r^{-1} b̃_{r1} ... introd. des λ ... Commutations des flèches ã_r, b̃_r, c̃_r aux λ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would document an early (c. 1978–80) combinatorial, dessin-indexed presentation of mapping class groupoids, predating or paralleling Hatcher–Thurston and Moore–Seiberg. It could be compared with Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps and with Grothendieck–Teichmüller actions on such groupoids. Its value depends on reconstructing the full set of relations from neighbouring pages.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows a concrete, apparently unpublished flag-indexed presentation scheme for a Teichmüller groupoid, with twist elements built as μ^∨μ. That is historically interesting, but the page is a fragmentary summary and the general idea (combinatorial presentations of mapping class groupoids) is well developed in later literature.
transcription_corrections: The line read as '𝓗 [?]' is most likely 'Il reste' ("it remains"), introducing the remaining relations (1) and (2').
Bottom line should read roughly: 'Commutations des flèches ã_r, b̃_r, c̃_r aux λ' — i.e. the transport relations (8),(9),(10) amount to commutation of the arrows with the λ's ('donnant λ').
Second line plausibly: 'les relations de transport (10) [sont] automatiques, (9) ⟶ 2, (8) ⟶ 1' (relation (9) reduces to (2), (8) to (1)).
B̃_r reads as B̃_r := ã_{r''}^{-1} b̃_{r1} b̃_r^{-1} (exponents uncertain).
The circled '3' at the top right is a page/sheet number, not equation (3).
